console.title: Private Invitation
console.subtitle: Random cover, character copy, and retention settings
console.api.title: API Settings
console.api.note: Shared: use SillyTavern's current API. Independent: request your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint through the SillyTavern backend.
console.api.profileManual: No profile selected (edit fields below directly)
console.api.fieldsNote: URL auto-completes /v1/chat/completions and is requested through the SillyTavern backend, so HTTPS pages can use HTTP API URLs. OpenAI-compatible endpoints only.
console.api.profileNoneSelected: Select a profile from the dropdown first.
console.api.fetchNeedUrl: Fill in the API URL first.
console.pool.title: Invitation Characters
console.pool.hint: Choose characters that can appear in homepage invitations. Empty selection means all characters.
console.pool.placeholder: Character name, card file, or character ID. One per line.
console.ai.charHint: Generate dialogue drafts for the character shown at the top. Switch character on the Copy tab.
console.ai.retentionCharHint: Generate retention drafts for the character shown at the top. Chat / world context is shared with the main flow.
console.control.title: Run Control
console.control.note: Trigger rules, global toggles, live preview.
console.control.globalNote: Common runtime toggles can be managed here too; no need to return to SillyTavern's extension settings.
console.control.continueNote: After you dismiss an invitation, auto-pick another character. Already-shown ones don't repeat in this round.
console.control.continuePickLimitNote: Round ends when the limit is hit, the pool runs out, or you accept an invitation.
console.control.panelThemeNote: Built-in plugin colors are used by default so the panel stays readable under bright or dark SillyTavern themes.
console.appearance.combinedNote: Layout, colors, motion and custom CSS all in one place.
console.appearance.advancedToggle: ✨ Design your own cover — custom CSS / AI writes CSS
console.pool.trigger.everyHome: Every time the homepage is shown
console.dialogue.title: Copy
console.charStyle.title: Per-character style override
console.charStyle.enabled: Use a custom look for this character
console.charStyle.note: When off, the global style applies. Only fields below override; empty / unchecked = inherit.
console.charStyle.autoAdapt: Auto-adapt text color for this character
console.charStyle.copied: Copied global style to this character.
console.dialogue.note: Each character has its own copy pool. AI drafts batches here from the character card, chat history, and lorebooks only, and never runs when the homepage invitation appears.
console.dialogue.badgeStyle: Custom appearance enabled for this character
console.copy.charactersNote: Pick one character — its dialogue pool and retention pool appear together below. The AI tab follows this selection.
console.copy.dialoguePoolNote: Lines drawn from here when the homepage invitation pops. Stored per character.
console.copy.retentionPoolNote: After the user dismisses the main invitation, a retention line may pop based on the chance below.
console.dialogue.poolInputPlaceholder: Type one line and press Enter or click Add (multi-line paste OK)
console.dialogue.poolNote: Click a chip to edit in place — Enter / blur to save. × removes a single line.
console.dialogue.poolEditHint: Click to edit, Enter to save, Esc to cancel
console.dialogue.poolEmpty: Pool is empty. Type one in, or harvest from the AI drafts.
console.dialogue.draftHint: Click + to move a line into the pool (and remove it from draft). Click × to drop from draft only. New generations append below — nothing gets wiped.
console.dialogue.draftEmpty: Draft list is empty. Click the button above to ask the AI.
console.dialogue.draftEmptyWarn: Draft list is empty. Generate some first.
console.dialogue.promptBodyPlaceholder: Edit the prompt directly. {char} becomes the character name, {count} becomes the batch size.
console.dialogue.maxTokensNote: Reasoning models (Gemini, DeepSeek-R) burn tokens thinking first. Raise this when output comes back empty (try 2400+).
console.dialogue.aiPromptPlaceholder: Add tone, relationship stage, or expressions to avoid. Use {char} for the character name.
console.dialogue.generateEmpty: AI returned no usable lines. For reasoning models (Gemini, DeepSeek-R), raise "Max tokens per call" to 2400+ and try again.
console.dialogue.generatedPlaceholder: AI output appears here first. One line per entry — the list below stays in sync.
console.dialogue.draftEmpty: Draft list is empty. Generate or paste lines first.
console.dialogue.noDraftSelected: Tick at least one draft line.
console.context.chatNote: Select chat files and generate in floor ranges. If no file is selected, the current chat is used.
console.context.chunkSummary: Each call sends: starting at "Start floor", up to "Floors per batch" lines, stopping at "End floor" (whichever is smaller). This is the main token control knob.
console.context.filterTagsPlaceholder: e.g. memory,summary — leave empty to inject the full chat
console.context.filterTagsNote: Only text wrapped in <tag>...</tag> is sent to the AI. Use comma to separate multiple tags. Leave empty to inject everything.
console.context.excludeTagsPlaceholder: e.g. thinking,system — leave empty to exclude nothing
console.context.excludeTagsNote: Strips <tag>...</tag> content from the chat first, then applies the filter. Use it to drop thinking blocks, system notes, etc.
console.context.worldNote: Select lorebooks to use during generation. This only reads content and does not edit lorebooks.
console.context.worldDefaultHint: Bound to this character card by default — pinned to top.
console.context.worldEntriesEmpty: No usable entries in this lorebook.
console.context.worldEntrySearch: Search entries, keys, or content in this lorebook
console.retention.title: Retention
console.retention.note: Retention has its own copy pool. When the homepage invitation is dismissed, these lines are sampled by chance.
console.retention.poolInputPlaceholder: Type one line and press Enter or click Add
console.retention.poolNote: For the second retention prompt after dismissal. Click a chip to edit; × removes a single line.
console.retention.draftHint: Click + to move a line into the retention pool (and remove from draft). Click × to drop from draft only. New generations append below.
console.retention.promptBodyPlaceholder: Edit the retention prompt directly. {char} becomes the character name, {count} becomes the batch size.
console.retention.aiPromptPlaceholder: Add retention intensity, relationship stage, or expressions to avoid. Use {char} for the character name.
console.retention.contextNote: Retention generation reuses the chat history and lorebook context selected on the Copy tab.
console.retention.generateEmpty: AI returned no usable retention lines
console.retention.generatedPlaceholder: AI output appears here first. One line per entry — the list below stays in sync.
console.retention.draftPick: Pick retention drafts to append / replace
console.style.title: Look
console.style.note: Choose barrage, bubble, or banner. Font size and color are configurable too.
console.style.bubblePositionNote: Pick a position on the 3×3 grid; nudge sliders below shift on top of it.
console.style.bubblePositionRatioWarn: ⚠️ Desktop card is roughly square (~1:1), mobile is a phone portrait (~9:19). The same position will look different on the two ends. Tune for the side you use most, then use the X/Y nudge sliders to compensate the other side.
console.style.bubbleOffsetNote: Positive = right / down, negative = left / up. Units are % of card width.
console.style.bubbleShapeNote: Different art styles suit different bubbles. Frameless mode strongly recommends auto-adapt or a text stroke.
console.style.autoAdaptColorNote: Reads cover image brightness and swaps text + stroke to a readable pair. Overrides manual color when on.
console.style.textStrokeNote: Adds an outline so text stays readable on any character art. 1-2px works well.
console.style.coverFitNote: On desktop, contain shrinks the image and the blurred backdrop bleeds around it — looks fuzzy. Cover modes crop edges for a sharper picture.
console.appearance.title: Appearance
console.appearance.note: Drop custom CSS here. Hook .pi-invitation-card / .pi-invitation-cover / .pi-invitation-message for your own filters or motion.
console.appearance.customCssNote: Injected into <style id="pi-custom-style">. Clear the box to remove all custom styles.
console.appearance.templateNote: Loading overwrites the current CSS. Save lets you name your current CSS and add it to "My templates" for later switching.
console.appearance.templateBodyEmpty: Current CSS is empty — nothing to save
console.appearance.clearCssConfirm: Clear the current custom CSS? This cannot be undone.
console.appearance.aiBrief: AI CSS — describe the look you want
console.appearance.aiBriefPlaceholder: e.g. Cool blue-purple neon border, glowing text, semi-transparent deep blue bubble.
console.appearance.aiBriefEmpty: Describe the style you want first.
console.appearance.aiEmpty: AI returned no usable CSS. Try again or rephrase.
console.appearance.aiDone: AI wrote CSS — overwrote the editor above.
console.appearance.aiFailed: AI CSS generation failed. Check token limit and SillyTavern backend.
console.appearance.aiNote: I'll feed AI the list of hookable nodes so it returns matching CSS, then overwrite the editor above. Tweak manually after.

invitation.notReady: SillyTavern is still loading, please try again in a moment.
invitation.defaultLine: A line from {char} drifts back again.
invitation.defaultRetentionLine: {char} is not ready to let you leave.
invitation.aiBatchInstruction: Generate {count} homepage character copy / memory lines for {char}.
invitation.retentionAiBatchInstruction: Generate {count} retention lines for {char}, used after the homepage invitation is dismissed.
invitation.aiOutputRules: Output rules: output exactly {count} lines. One line per item. No numbering, no explanation, no quotation marks. Do not write ads, customer-service greetings, or direct chat solicitation. Avoid direct calls such as "come find me", "click in", "chat with me", or "enter the chat". Focus on memory, character voice, story hooks, and unfinished emotional tension.
invitation.retentionAiOutputRules: Output rules: output exactly {count} retention lines. One line per item. No numbering, no explanation, no quotation marks. Do not repeat ordinary invitation copy. Do not write ads, customer-service greetings, or forceful commands. This is the second line after rejection: restrained, unfinished, reluctant, emotionally resonant, and story-aware. Light retention is allowed, but avoid oily solicitation.
invitation.promptPreset.memoryFlashback: Memory flashback: The lines should feel like sudden fragments from things the user and character once experienced together: an old echo, a signature moment, a remembered wound, or an unfinished line. Prioritize personality, relationship tension, past plot traces, and world keywords.
invitation.promptPreset.signatureScene: Signature scene: The goal is not to invite the user, but to make them instantly think, "this is something this character would say." Use signature-scene lines, restrained monologue, provocation, tenderness, obsession, memory fragments, or unfinished promises.
invitation.promptPreset.oldChatEcho: Old chat echo: The lines should feel like they surfaced from a past conversation, a plot node, or a relationship shift. Emphasize memory, relationship texture, and incompletion rather than inviting the user into chat.
invitation.promptPreset.worldFragment: World fragment: The lines should read like plot remnants, character memories, worldbuilding clues, or something the character left for the user. Prioritize the character's world, past events, relationship tension, secrets, obsessions, and unfinished story threads.
invitation.promptPreset.emotionalHook: Low-solicitation emotional hook: The copy only creates memory, character voice, and story hooks. It should feel like something the character once said, might say, or something that belongs only to this relationship. It may be intimate, dangerous, nostalgic, broken, provocative, or tender.
invitation.retentionPromptPreset.lastWhi: Last whisper: A restrained line left behind after the user refuses, as if from behind a door, in the rain, or from the other side of the screen. Keep it quiet and lingering, not a direct demand to return.
invitation.retentionPromptPreset.unfinis: Unfinished promise: Tie the retention line to an unresolved promise, plot thread, secret, wound, or relationship moment between the character and user. Make it feel like one thing is still unfinished.
invitation.retentionPromptPreset.softRef: Restrained retention: The character does not force the user to stay. They show reluctance in a way that fits their personality: tender, awkward, proud, controlled, cold, or broken.
invitation.retentionPromptPreset.jealous: Possessive afterglow: A little possessiveness, jealousy, testing, or reluctance is allowed, but it must fit the character and must not sound like advertising or solicitation.
invitation.retentionPromptPreset.storyCl: Story cliffhanger: Use world context, old chat echoes, character secrets, or imminent story movement as the second hook. The point is not begging the user to stay, but making the unfinished story visible.
